title: Reconcile partial-token accounting for streamed attachments with client-specified chunk boundaries
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem summary: Customers that stream binary or text attachments (multipart or application/octet-stream) over long-lived websocket/HTTP chunked connections sometimes get overcharged or undercharged due to misaligned token boundaries between client-sent chunks and server-side tokenization. Root causes observed include: clients splitting UTF-8 codepoints or BPE tokens across frames, base64 vs raw encodings changing length expectations, server-side early prefix-caching that counts bytes instead of canonical tokens, and echo/sideband messages (e.g., progress pings) being included in token tallies. This ticket defines a deterministic canonicalization and aggregation strategy so that the metering pipeline attributes the exact same tokens regardless of client chunking or framing semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
- Streaming requests with chunk boundaries split inside tokens must produce identical final token counts as the equivalent single-request submission.
- Attachment encoding variants (raw, base64, chunked multipart) normalize to the same token counts for identical logical content.
- No billing delta >0.5% observed in a synthetic 100k request audit between current and new canonicalization on non-edge cases; for edge-case fuzz inputs, discrepancies must be explainable and logged.
- System maintains idempotent attribution: replaying the same frames (with same idempotency key) does not double-bill.
- All changes behind a runtime flag and deployed as canary before global rollout.
implementation_plan:
1) Add a canonical chunk-aggregator component in the edge ingestion path that buffers up to X bytes or until a logical delimiter, and exposes canonical byte ranges to the tokenizer.
2) Implement 'tokenization handshake' metadata on session start: client can declare encoding (raw|base64|multipart) and optional chunk-boundary-hint. If absent, server selects safe defaults.
3) Update tokenizer wrapper to operate on canonicalized buffers and emit a stable 'token-provenance' list (token_id + source-range) used by the metering ledger.
4) Modify metering ledger to attribute tokens by token-provenance instead of frame offsets; include idempotency keys for partial-finalization.
5) Add a fallback reconciliation task that detects mismatches between provisional and finalized attribution and emits auto-credit events for confirmed client misreports.
6) Feature flag and staged rollout with canary on internal tenants then 5% of production workloads.
Notes on trade-offs: buffering increases head-of-line latency for tiny fragments—we'll keep a small max-buffer (e.g., 256B or 50ms) and expose analytics to tune per-customer QoS.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: tokenizer wrapper with split-token boundaries, base64 decode path, multipart boundaries.
- Property/fuzz tests: generate UTF-8 and BPE split scenarios, random frame splits, verify canonical counts match single-shot tokenization.
- Integration tests: end-to-end streaming client simulator sends identical logical payloads with different chunking styles and validates billing ledger outputs.
- Load test: 10k concurrent long-lived streams with attachments, measure latency and billing variance.
- Audit test: run a 100k synthetic-job audit comparing old vs new ledger attribution and generate discrepancy report.
- QA checklist: validate idempotency on reconnect, resume, and aborted streams; verify credits created for reconciled overcharges.
migration_plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable flag for internal and 5% prod. Monitor discrepancies and latency.
- Phase 2 (wider rollout): enable flag for 50% with auto-credit reconciliation enabled.
- Phase 3 (full): switch canonical attribution as default, keep reconciliation for 30 days to auto-correct historical mismatches.
- Billing: for any customer-facing corrected overcharge >$5, create automatic credit and send an explanatory digest.
- Data retention: keep provisional -> final mapping for 90 days for audits.
progress_updates:
2026-03-02: Triage meeting - confirmed reproducible overcharge on multipart base64 test harness; assigned to Diego.
2026-03-04: Spike completed on buffering heuristics (256B/50ms). Measured +4ms p95 latency on internal load.
2026-03-06: Tokenizer wrapper prototype emits token-provenance ranges; unit tests for split-token cases added.
2026-03-09: Metrology: defined auditing queries to detect provisional vs final mismatches and sample dashboard metrics.
2026-03-11: Implementation PR opened for canonical chunk-aggregator (see linked_prs). Awaiting eng review re idempotency contraction logic.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed the design doc; no secrets exposure concerns but recommended KMS audit for any persisted idempotency mapping.
blockers: Open questions: 1) Should we accept client-declared encoding as authoritative or always re-canonicalize on server? (engineering prefers server-canonical by default). 2) Need product sign-off on acceptable latency trade-offs for small-chunk streaming customers. 3) Final reconciliation policy for ambiguous fragments (requires billing/legal input).
